challenges.name: unions-narrowing-quiz
challenges.title: Predict it: undefined, 0 and narrowing
challenges.description: Find the falsy-zero trap in a template string, then pick the ways to read a value that might be undefined that both compile under --strict and never throw.

questions.explanation: || returns its right side whenever the left side is falsy, and 0 is falsy just like undefined, null, "" and NaN. So eta || "a few" is "a few" for eta = 0, and the courier who is already at the door is shown as arriving in a few minutes. The code compiles: eta || "a few" has the type number | string, which a template string accepts. Use eta ?? "a few" (only null and undefined fall through) or test eta === undefined explicitly.

questions.question: const courier = couriers.find((c) => c.id === id); gives courier the type Courier | undefined. Which lines compile with tsc --strict AND never throw at runtime? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: courier?.name ?? "unassigned" stops at undefined and supplies a fallback. if (courier) and an early return on courier === undefined both narrow courier to Courier for the code that reads .name. courier.name is error TS18048 ('courier' is possibly 'undefined'). courier!.name compiles because ! tells the checker to trust you, and throws the exact TypeError of the incident when find returns undefined. courier !== null does not remove undefined from the type (find never returns null), so courier.name inside it is still error TS18048.

challenges.name: fix-tracking-undefined-courier
challenges.title: Fix the tracking page that crashes on a missing courier
challenges.description: The Chợ Sớm tracking page crashed with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'name')" for every order whose courier had left the company. In TypeScript the same code does not even compile: couriers.find returns Courier | undefined. Fix trackingLine by narrowing (no ! operator): an order without a courier is waiting for one, a courier who is not in the list is not available, an ETA of null means the courier is on the way and an ETA of 0 means the courier is at the door. The test runner reads the couriers and the orders as JSON and prints one line per order.
